US oil refiners are set for an economic boom.

The S&P 500 Oil & Gas Refining & Marketing index is now up +108% in 12 months, to ~3,250 points, near its all-time high.

The index tracks large US companies involved in refining, marketing, and transporting oil and gas.

This marks its largest 12-month increase since the 2020 pandemic recovery.

Over the last 30 years, the only other comparable periods of strength were recorded in 2013 and 2005.

Since April 2025, oil and gas refining stocks have surged a massive +175%.

Markets are bracing for a US oil refining surge.

BREAKING: Global broad money supply surged +$10.7 trillion YoY in June, or +7.7%, to a record $150 trillion.

This marks the 9th consecutive YoY increase above +7.0%, the longest such streak since 2021.

The biggest increase over this period was recorded in February 2026, at +11.9%.

Since 2000, global money supply has risen +$124 trillion, a +6.9% compounded annual growth rate over this period.

Since 2020 alone, money supply has surged +$50 trillion, or +50%, equivalent to an average increase of ~$7.5 trillion per year.

Global money creation is expanding at a historic pace.

tweets.text:
Private credit's weakest borrowers are starting to crack.

When a company is too strained to pay interest in cash, it tacks the interest onto the loan instead. That is PIK, and lenders charge extra for it because only the shakiest borrowers need it.

Now look at the split. Yields on normal BDC loans have fallen since early 2025. Yields on PIK loans bottomed and turned back up, led by software.

Lenders want more to hold the weakest paper and less from everyone else. That widening gap is how a credit cycle starts to roll over, and credit rolls over before stocks do.

Scott Bessent tried to rescue the bond market. It lasted 12 days.

On Aug 19 the Treasury Secretary shocked traders by expanding bond buybacks to force long yields down. It worked, briefly. By Sept 1 the 30-year yield was right back to 5.27%, the exact level it sat at before he acted. The 10-year is even higher now, at 4.80%, a level last seen before Trump took office.

This is the bond market telling Washington that a buyback tweak does not fix a supply problem. The US is financing nearly $40 trillion in debt and running a $2 trillion deficit, and buyers demand more to hold it. Bessent once said the bond market has taken out more governments than howitzers. It just erased his own rescue.

You cannot jawbone away a debt problem. Until the deficit shrinks, every long-bond rally is a fade, and the cost keeps passing through to every mortgage priced off the 10-year. $TLT

The US Treasury is issuing less long-term debt this year. Long yields are climbing anyway. The new flood of supply is coming from somewhere else.

Wall Street expects corporate bond supply to swell by about $474 billion in 2026, almost all of it tech giants funding AI. Investment-grade firms have already sold nearly $1.5 trillion this year, up 36%. The biggest tech borrowers alone now equal roughly 25% of the Treasury's net issuance, 5x their share a year ago.

This is crowding out in reverse. For decades the government was the whale in the bond market. Now the hyperscalers are issuing so much long-dated debt to build data centers that they compete with Uncle Sam for the same buyers. BofA estimates it has already added about 30 basis points to the 10-year yield this year.

So long rates keep climbing even with the Fed on hold. The driver is a record wave of new bonds the market has to absorb, and that cost lands on every mortgage and corporate loan priced off the 10-year. $TLT

The house always wins. Now there is a number on it.

Bank of America tracked the cash flowing to online betting platforms this year. For every dollar bettors deposited, they pulled back less than 75 cents. Every single month. The recovery ratio never once touched breakeven.

Gen Z has decided that betting is investing.

Gen Z and Millennials made up 88% of online betting activity in July, with Gen Z alone at 48%, per Bank of America. And Gen Z is twice as likely as older generations to call sports betting an investment. 1 in 5 bettors already treat it like an asset class.

This is what happens when a generation meets markets through apps that feel exactly like a sportsbook. The parlay and the options ticket live on the same phone, sold the same way. One of them pays back less than 75 cents on the dollar, and they are calling it a portfolio.

A generation that mistakes a wager for an investment learns the difference the expensive way. That is the retirement problem hiding inside the gambling boom.
